data.name: Raish
data.gender_notes: Raish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Raish is a name derived from the Hindu god Ra, who is the god of the sun. The name Raish signifies the power, strength and leadership qualities associated with the sun god. The name Raish carries the meaning “Sun God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Raish usually hope their child will grow to embody sun god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Raish is a spiritual name that represents the sun god and the power, strength and leadership qualities associated with him.
data.etymology: Raish belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sun God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Raish total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Raish holds significant cultural relevance in Hinduism as it is derived from the name of one of the primary deities, Lord Ra. This connection imbues the name with a sense of proud Hindu heritage and a strong foundation in Hindu mythology.
data.spiritual_significance: Beyond its cultural significance, the name Raish holds deep spiritual meaning as it is a reminder of the immense power, strength, and leadership qualities of Lord Ra, the sun god. The name Raish invokes the power of the sun, signifying enlightenment, growth, and protection. In essence, the name Raish serves as a constant reminder of the divine presence of Lord Ra and the strength, power, and wisdom associated with him.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Raish is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Rajas', meaning passion or emotion. It is believed that individuals named Raish are deeply connected to their feelings and are driven by their desires, making them passionate and vibrant individuals.

historical_references.reference: Rajasthan royal inscriptions mention Raish, a Jaina monk who was a contemporary of Hemachandra Suri (1089-1173 AD). He is believed to have composed Jaina works, including the 'Tattvartha Sutra Bhagavata' commentary.

The Kannada inscriptions of Hampi refer to Raish, who was a Jaina Tirthankara (a spiritual leader). He is believed to have lived during the 12th century AD and is considered a significant figure in Jaina history.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Raish' is derived from the Hindu god, Ra. Ra is associated with the sun and represents power, creation, and nourishment. In modern contexts, the name 'Raish' can be found across various platforms. On Instagram, there are multiple accounts dedicated to Hindu mythology that feature the god Ra and his symbol, the sun, in their posts. On Twitter, users often discuss astrological aspects related to the sun sign 'Leo' and reference Ra as the god of that sign. Lastly, on Pinterest, 'Raish' can be seen as a popular name for fashion accessories inspired by the sun symbol or as a name for sun-themed home decor.
